issue.title: Implement Android Oak client

repository.name: oak
repository.description: Meaningful control of data in distributed systems.

issue.body:
Something like

https://github.com/project-oak/oak/blob/39838c8b71dd42731615ebdb09f4d15924e53ec9/oak/client/application_client.h#L47

but usable by Android applications.

I am not sure whether this means it should be implemented natively in Java, or have a thin Java wrapper around the C++ client, or whether we can just offer the C++ version and assume that Android applications will wrap it.

In any case, it requires establishing a channel using [EKEP](https://asylo.dev/docs/concepts/ekep.html).

I note though that there is already a separate [Android gRPC stack](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/connectivity/grpc), but it does not seem to be as flexible as the regular gRPC stack. In particular, I am not sure it offers any way of using different channel credentials.

@ipetr0v could you start looking into it, and seeing what else is missing? e.g., can we use bazel with a different configuration to check whether some of our targets can be built for Android?

cc @annasapek @KeithMoyer

issue.body:
This change adds `ares_android.h` and `ares_android.c` to `third_party/cares/cares.BUILD` in order to support builds in the Android Native Development Kit (NDK).

Fixes #21437
